conflicts.about: Whether the declaration page checks the notification is complete.

positions.says: A declaration that passes every check but whose notification is not ready to submit is refused and returns to the review marked as refused.
A real validation constraint overrides the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: Design Release 2.1's declaration page does no completeness check of its own and can be opened directly (prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-130, weighed in the review-and-submit area). The ruling's validation override wins for the submit: it keeps the re-check, and the page is reached only by the review's own Continue, so a typed address goes to the review instead (req-922). Nothing of the prototype's look and feel is set aside; what goes is the ability to open the page unchecked, which is a validation matter rather than a design one.

conflicts.about: Whether identifier-driven outstanding items (the confirmation bullet, the action-required warnings and error, and the dashboard's 'Information is missing') are built now, and what makes identifiers incomplete.

positions.says: Whether DR1's every-identifier rule or V4's at-least-one rule governs inc-103 is undecided; only the design authority can say.
A notification with required but incomplete identifiers that meets the submission minimum is submitted with the item 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification'.
The confirmation page lists the identifier item when any commodity line has fewer identified animals than it needs.
One identifier is enough: DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built, its blocker is removed, and these requirements are weighed against the one-identifier rule.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first and settles it: an animal record counts as identified once one identifier is filled, inc-103 is closed, and the identifier-driven items are built with no blocker. Design Release 2.1 settles the rest: identifiers are incomplete when a line whose species asks for identifiers holds fewer identified records than the animals it declares, which includes the single-species consignment with none saved (DR1's p8-062 case). The confirmation bullet is built and proven (req-931, repo-frontend-p7-065, repo-tests-p3-028 and p3-029); the action-required warnings and the list marking that also rested on this rule are withdrawn by the 16 November ruling (c-410), not by this one. The DR1 hold, its undecided zero-record timing and the notes' open question are set aside.

conflicts.about: Which list 'Return to your dashboard' and the viewed notification's Back link go to.

positions.says: The dashboard is temporary in the animals frontend and moves to the INS front door.
The confirmation's 'Return to your dashboard' goes to the overall dashboard at the release's root.
'Return to your dashboard' goes to the service's own dashboard, where the notification list is shown.
The view's Back link and the confirmation's return link are kept, as c-143 set them.
Every page Design Release 2.1 sends to the overall dashboard goes to the set's own notification list: the view's Back link and the confirmation's 'Return to your dashboard' among them.
The live animals notification list stays in the animals frontend and is not moved to the INS frontend in this programme.
The move of the animals notification list to the INS frontend, kept from DR1 by the morning ruling, no longer applies in this programme.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first, with claim 3 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates: 'Return to your dashboard' on the confirmation page and a viewed notification's Back link both go to the set's own notification list in its own frontend, the live-animals set root for live animals, the germinal products set root for germinal products and plants' own list for plants, which repo-frontend-p6-008, p7-073 and repo-plantsfrontend-p10-010 and p11-054 now do. The INS front door is reached through the service navigation as today. This replaces the earlier outcome that sent both links to the INS front door's dashboard, which the morning ruling kept, so that claim is overruled. The prototype's 'overall dashboard' is read as the set's own list, so its link positions still back the links' place on the page. DR1's note that the dashboard moves to the INS front door is not listed as overruled because it still backs the address book's place in the INS front door; for these two links it no longer applies.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the real mechanism stays, looking and reading as Design Release 2.1's link. The prototype's GET link to its start page is not built.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a template never offers a declaration, because its review would end with 'Save template', so the guards are not built. The 4 November ruling then parks templates altogether (c-413), so nothing of them is built in this programme.

conflicts.about: Whether the notification submitted page's ITAHC rule reaches the germinal-products set and plants.

positions.says: The germinal products copy of the notification submitted page names a missing ITAHC on the same condition as the live-animals page.
Plants' confirmation page gains no outstanding-items list and no certificate item.
The Notification submitted page lists the ITAHC as still to upload whenever no ITAHC was uploaded, whatever other documents were uploaded.
That decision is stated for live animals pages only, so whether the equivalent germinal-products and plants pages behave the same way is left open.
Plants' confirmation page tells the notifier nothing about what happens next and lists nothing outstanding.

conflicts.outcome: The 27 November ruling ranks first and keeps the question's default: the germinal products copy of the confirmation page names a missing ITAHC on the same condition as the live-animals page (req-declaration-and-submitted-002), and plants' confirmation gains no outstanding-items list and no certificate item (req-2024), since plants has no ITAHC. The 26 October rule stands for live animals (req-929). Nothing is overruled: the 26 October gap claim only records that the earlier ruling was silent, and plants' today claim is what the ruling keeps.
